# Macro Regime

## TL;DR

**Strongly risk-on and improving.** The Dow Jones crossed 50,000 for the first time ever on May 7, 2026. S&P 500 at 7,377 (+0.17%) and Nasdaq at 25,977 (+0.53%) — both at all-time highs intraday. US-Iran peace deal is materially advancing: Iran expected to deliver its 14-point response to the US peace proposal today (May 7), lifting risk sentiment strongly. Oil has pulled back to $94-97/bbl from $100+ peak. AMD Q1 2026 blowout (+38% YoY revenue, EPS +43%) confirms the AI capex supercycle. AI semiconductor stocks continue to lead the broad rally. Regime assessment: **strongly risk-on**, with the two remaining headwinds being Kevin Warsh Fed succession (May 15, hawkish tightening-bias tail) and final signing of the Iran MOU. [sources: web_research/GOOG.json macro_context, run 20260507_164625; web_research/NVDA.json macro_context, run 20260507_123732]

## Fed posture

The Federal Reserve voted to hold the federal funds rate at **3.50%–3.75%** on April 29 (8-4 dissent — most lopsided since October 1992). Chair Powell's tenure ended; Kevin Warsh is the leading successor candidate (hawkish, Senate confirmation pending May 15). Market pricing: zero cuts through 2026 and only one 25bp cut projected for 2026 total. The Warsh succession introduces policy uncertainty independent of the rate level — growth stocks including NVDA, AMZN, GOOG, AAPL, and META are most exposed to tightening-bias repricing. Oil pulling back from $100+ to $94-97/bbl is a meaningful disinflationary signal; if Iran deal finalizes and oil settles below $90, the Fed hold timeline could shorten materially. [source: web_research/GOOG.json macro_context, 20260507_164625]

## Rate trajectory and inflation

Inflation above 2% target but improving: oil falling from $100+ peak toward $94-97/bbl on Iran ceasefire progress is a direct energy disinflation driver. If Iran deal finalizes and oil settles below $90, June 2026 Fed meeting rate cut probability rises. US midterm election uncertainty adds further policy noise in H2 2026. [source: web_research/GOOG.json, 20260507_164625]

## Market context (May 7, 2026)

**Dow Jones crossed 50,000 for the first time ever on May 7.** S&P 500 at 7,377 (+0.17%) and Nasdaq at 25,977 (+0.53%) — all-time highs intraday. AMD Q1 2026 earnings (May 5 AMC): revenue $10.25B +38% YoY, EPS $1.37 +43%, Q2 guide $11.2B beats $10.5B consensus — direct AI capex supercycle confirmation. AI semiconductor stocks leading the broad rally (AMD +17.77%, Supermicro +24.5%, Nvidia +5.5% on May 6-7). US non-farm payrolls report due May 8 — macro watch item. [source: web_research/GOOG.json macro_context, 20260507_164625; web_research/NVDA.json, 20260507_123732]

## Geopolitical and regulatory

**Iran-US conflict: actively de-escalating, final stage.** Iran expected to deliver 14-point response to US peace proposal on May 7 — markets have priced meaningful advance, lifting risk sentiment strongly. Oil at $94-97/bbl, down from $100+ peak. Strait of Hormuz closure threat remains a live left-tail if talks collapse, but probability continues to fall. Additional flashpoints: US-Venezuela tensions, NATO Greenland posture, tariff uncertainty. Fed leadership transition May 15 is the most proximate near-term policy risk. [source: web_research/GOOG.json macro_context, 20260507_164625]

## Risk-off triggers

- **Iran ceasefire collapse** — talks fail, oil re-spikes above $100, energy inflation re-accelerates
- **Kevin Warsh hawkish confirmation signal (May 15)** — tighter-for-longer re-rates growth stocks lower
- **AI capex ROI disappointment** — any major infrastructure player signals wasted GPU spend
- **US non-farm payrolls surprise (May 8)** — hot jobs data could re-price rate cut expectations
- **US tariff escalation** — additional rounds pressure supply chains and consumer sentiment

## Last updated

2026-05-07. Updated by run `20260507_164625`. Key changes from prior run 20260507_123732: Dow Jones crossed 50,000 for first time (new milestone); S&P 500 updated to 7,377 intraday (from 7,365.12 May 6 close); Nasdaq updated to 25,977 intraday (from 25,838.94 May 6 close); oil updated to $94-97/bbl (vs $91.73 in prior run — slight discrepancy in sources; Iran 14-point response delivery expected May 7). Regime assessment: strongly risk-on, unchanged. Warsh May 15 remains single primary tail risk.

thesis_tldr.content:
SanDisk printed a blowout Q3 FY2026 (2026-04-30): $5.95B revenue (+251% YoY), 78.4% GAAP gross margin, $1.47B datacenter revenue (+645% YoY), five multi-year hyperscaler contracts, $42B minimum revenue backlog, zero net debt. Stock has since run to ~$1,406 intraday — above the sell-side average PT of ~$1,250 (range $650–$2,000 post-earnings revisions; source: web_research/SNDK.json analyst_consensus, run 20260505_211609). Despite exceptional top-line growth, operating margins remain negative (-18.7% operating, -22.3% net; source: signals_combined.json fundamentals_analyst_agent SNDK, run 20260505_211609). The prior thesis was "blowout fundamentals vs. stretched valuation"; the valuation case has now worsened — price has overrun even the most bullish prior PTs. No entry exists until pullback to ~$1,072–$1,100 (10 EMA zone).

**Prior thesis claim falsified this run:** The bootstrap note that the stock traded "within or above the buy consensus range" at ~$1,187 has been superseded — at $1,406, SNDK now trades well above the sell-side average PT ($1,250) and has been downgraded as "overheated" by Seeking Alpha (2026-05-05; source: web_research/SNDK.json ticker_news).

## Lessons

2026-04-30 | NVDA | EMA pullback Fib dip-buy | -$63.20 (corrected from -$264.65) | Stop triggered at $205.30 (hourly Fib 61.8%); swing_trend_momentum and swing_breakout were bullish on AI capex thesis, but price breached the stop zone intraday amid stretched macro (RSI 81–87) with no bullish confirmation candle before exit. **Note:** trade was originally sized 67 shares ($14,020) due to a phantom $100K budget bug (fixed commit b2b472d). With the correct $25K budget at 14.2% vol-adj limit, position would have been 16 shares ($3,348). Corrected P&L reflects the strategy's actual signal quality, not the sizing error.
2026-05-04 | AMZN | mean-reversion fade short | OUTCOME: -$10.14 | Mean-reversion short thesis (April 30 shooting star, RSI 82–88) stopped at $276 as extreme ADX 65 trend absorbed the reversal; swing_mean_reversion recommended the setup but the regime (ADX 60+) sets an elevated bar for fading overbought conditions confirmed by identical NVDA stop-out April 30.
2026-05-05 | DIS | pre-earnings breakout long | OUTCOME: -$4.99 | Pre-earnings breakout above $103 (4/5 swing agents bullish, swing_breakout and swing_trend_momentum) invalidated by macro reversal (Iran escalation May 4, WTI +$105) that converted the April 30 risk-on tailwind into a risk-off headwind; sub-threshold entry volume (1.23x vs. 1.5x minimum) was an early warning sign.
2026-05-06 | GOOG | mean-reversion fade short | OUTCOME: -$6.50 | Mean-reversion short (RSI-7 90.69, Z-score 2.56) stopped at $389.50 as ADX 74.23 extreme trend absorbed the fade; swing_mean_reversion recommended the setup but the regime repeated the NVDA/AMZN pattern — ADX 60+ environments make fading overbought conditions highly unreliable; strongly risk-on macro (S&P ATH, US-Iran MOU) added upside momentum.
2026-05-06 | AMD | statistical exhaustion short | OUTCOME: -$17.82 | Mean-reversion short (Z-score 2.6, RSI 83, +74% 21d surge) gap-stopped at $372.31 when Q1 2026 earnings blowout (+38% YoY, EPS +43%) gapped AMD +15% overnight; swing_mean_reversion and swing_catalyst_news recommended the fade but earnings binary created a non-linear gap-through-stop outcome; half-sizing to 1 share limited damage to -$17.82 vs -$35.64.
